items.title: Just Seven of 17 Ward 7 Hopefuls Show Up to Answer Voters' Questions in Mississauga
items.summary: According to a report from mississauga.com, only seven of the seventeen candidates running for Mississauga's Ward 7 council seat turned up for a public meeting where residents could question them directly. The Sept. 14 event, organized by the Applewood Heights and Hills Residents' Association, drew more than 30 attendees to the Royal Canadian Legion branch on Dundas Street. Topics ranged from crime and affordability to concerns over e-scooters in the ward. Adad, a former manager with Safe City Mississauga who spent a decade working in crime prevention and the non-profit sector, told the crowd he wants candidates to move past short-term election promises and focus on longer-term solutions. Alves, a former Peel District School Board trustee, argued that new housing developments in the area have not been planned with Ward 7 families in mind. The low turnout among candidates left many residents' questions unanswered by more than half the field seeking the seat. With the Oct. 26 municipal election approaching, voters looking for direct answers from candidates may need to seek out other forums before voting day.

items.title: Mississauga Opens Early Voting Options Starting Oct. 6 Ahead of Election Day
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents wanting to skip the lines on election day can start casting an early ballot on Oct. 6. The first stretch of advance voting, running Oct. 6 to 7, is limited to a single location at the Mississauga Civic Centre on City Centre Drive. Starting Oct. 8, advance polling expands to all 11 ward locations across the city, running through Oct. 11. Voters are not restricted to their own ward during this period and may cast a ballot at any available site. City officials note that this flexibility applies only during the advance voting window, not on election day itself. Voting day proper falls on Oct. 26, when residents must return to their assigned polling location. The expanded advance schedule gives Mississauga voters five extra days beyond election day itself to make their choice known.

items.title: Mayoral Debate Reveals Rare Consensus on a New Parking Garage for Troubled Ridgeway Plaza
items.summary: According to INsauga, the idea of building a four-storey parking garage behind Ridgeway Plaza came up Friday afternoon during Mississauga's first mayoral debate of the election season, held at Sheridan College's Hazel McCallion Campus. A moderator asked the four main candidates what they would do to make the west-end plaza, home to roughly 115 restaurants, more pedestrian and traffic friendly. Incumbent Carolyn Parrish, who won a mayoral byelection in June 2024 after Bonnie Crombie left for provincial politics, pointed to a large plot of land behind the plaza and said a paid parking facility there would pay for itself within three to four years. INsauga reports that while the four candidates, who also included city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, disagreed on most issues during the nearly two-hour debate, they largely agreed on building a new parking garage at Ridgeway Plaza. Crombie, who served as Mississauga's mayor from 2014 to 2024 before leaving to lead the Ontario Liberal Party, told the debate audience she is concerned for residents living near the plaza who have dealt with noise and other problems in recent years.

items.title: A Carolyn Parrish surprise and 3 other key takeaways from the Mississauga mayoral debate
items.summary: Incumbent mayor claims she has convinced Premier Doug Ford to change the Peel police funding formula. The Mississauga mayoral debate hosted by CBC and the Mississauga Board of Trade on Friday featured some unexpected claims about the police funding formula. Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish says she has convinced Premier Doug Ford to fix the Peel police funding formula that she argues has left Mississauga residents unfairly paying more than Brampton for years. Parrish made the claim on the stage of the first mayoral debate of the campaign Friday afternoon, after facing criticism for resigning from the Peel police board, a decision she has defended as necessary to challenge unprecedented police budget increase requests. Parrish said she met the premier at his home six weeks ago and that he committed to making the change when the legislature reconvenes in November. ’ And he said ... ‘November, when the house is back in session,’” Parrish told reporters after the debate. ” She said isn’t sure what the exact proposal would be though she’d be happy with a 50-50 split over the current 62-38 that leaves the bulk of the cost on Mississauga taxpayers, she said. items.title: Thousands of Salmon Push Upstream Through the Credit River as Mississauga's Annual Run Gets Underway
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, an annual salmon run is now underway in the Credit River, drawing thousands of fish swimming upstream from Lake Ontario in what the city calls an annual phenomenon. The city says the run typically begins each September in Mississauga, as well as in parts of Brampton and Caledon, and continues through the end of October, usually peaking in early October. INsauga reports that some of the best spots in the city to witness the event include Erindale Park, The Riverwood Conservancy's Riverwood Park and Meadowvale Conservation Area. According to the city, the salmon push against the current of the Credit River each late summer and early fall to spawn and lay their eggs. City officials explain that as water temperatures cool and fall rains raise water levels, freshwater salmon begin their yearly trek from the mouth of Lake Ontario up the Credit River to spawn. The city encourages residents of all ages to come witness the natural event for themselves.

items.title: Feasibility Study on the Table as Crombie Pitches a Subway Extension Into Mississauga's City Centre
items.summary: According to the Star, Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie is pitching an extension of Toronto's Bloor-Danforth subway line from Kipling station into Mississauga's city centre. Crombie says that if elected, she would commission a feasibility study and lobby both the province and federal government to help fund the project, framing it as the kind of large infrastructure investment governments are currently looking to back. She pointed out that Vaughan already has subway service and that lines are being planned for Markham and Richmond Hill, arguing Mississauga should not be left out. The Hurontario light rail line, also known as the Hazel McCallion line, is currently under construction and was chosen years ago partly because the region's density did not yet justify a subway. Crombie argues that density has since grown enough to support a larger investment. Incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish, who is also running for re-election, has floated the idea of a Mississauga subway before but has pointed to a price tag of roughly a billion dollars per kilometre as a major obstacle unless Queen's Park covers most of the cost. Parrish did not respond to a request for comment on Crombie's specific proposal.

items.title: City Weighs a Second 'Signature Park' Just North of Kariya Park in Mississauga's Downtown Core
items.summary: According to INsauga, the City of Mississauga is exploring plans for what staff describe as a possible second signature park in the city's downtown core, just steps north of the existing Kariya Park. City staff wrote in a report going to council on Tuesday that the new greenspace could become a distinctive and memorable public space and a focal point for residents and visitors in the Downtown Core. The proposed site sits at the corner of Burnhamthorpe Road West and Kariya Drive, though at just under one acre it would be significantly smaller than Kariya Park itself. Raj Sheth, the city's commissioner of community services, said in the report that the new park's proximity to Kariya Park, already regarded as one of the city's most treasured public spaces, offers a chance to complement and enhance the broader park experience in that part of downtown. Staff are recommending the city enter into a memorandum of understanding with developer Camrost Felcor to explore an enhanced park design for the city-owned property at that southwest corner, according to INsauga. The greenspace under consideration sits adjacent to a site Camrost Felcor is currently developing.

items.title: Weekly Yard Waste Pickup Returns This Fall as Peel Region Preps a Bigger Service Handoff to Brampton
items.summary: According to INsauga, weekly yard waste pickup is set to begin again this fall across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon, with residents able to check their own collection calendar or sign up for free reminders to find their pickup day. Acceptable yard waste includes leaves, yard rakings with debris, tree trimmings and branches, brush and hedge clippings, household and garden plants, and Halloween pumpkins without the candle, INsauga reports. The outlet notes grass clippings are not accepted either at the curb or at Community Recycling Centres, and all yard waste at the curb must go in kraft paper bags or reusable containers clearly marked as yard waste, since plastic bags are not accepted. Looking further ahead, INsauga reports that starting in October of next year, the City of Brampton will take over garbage, organics and yard waste collection for both Brampton and Caledon, a service currently handled by the Region of Peel. According to INsauga, that shift is part of a broader provincial restructuring of services across Peel Region that is moving several responsibilities from the regional government to Brampton, Caledon and Mississauga.
